lessons.title: Am I allowed to?
lessons.subtitle: The approval decision in a few questions

concept.body:
Shadow AI means AI use for work outside approved tools and controls. It includes private chat accounts, browser extensions, new AI features in software you bought long ago, and personal API keys. Such workflows often lack a contract, permissions, retention rules and a reporting route.

Article 4 of the EU AI Act has applied since 2 February 2025. Since the amendment by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, providers and deployers must take measures to support the development of AI literacy of their staff, matched to knowledge, context of use and affected people. The article prescribes no particular course format or certificate.

Day to day this means: before any new use you check tool, purpose, data class and approval. An incident is reported, not deleted.
concept.takeaway: Check tool, purpose, data class and approval first. When in doubt, ask; when something goes wrong, report.

exercise.title: Decide three realistic situations
exercise.instructions: Work through the questions for each case. At the end you see whether your outcome fits the case and why.

options.label: I want to use an AI tool for a task.
Data has already gone into an unapproved tool.

nodes.question: Is the tool approved in this edition and configuration?

options.label: Yes, it is on the approval list.
No, or I do not know.

nodes.question: Is the purpose approved for this tool?
What data class is the input?
Is the tool explicitly approved for confidential data?
Does the purpose need every detail you want to enter?

options.label: No, there is more in it.

results.title: Go ahead, with review
results.body: Approved tool, approved purpose, matching data class, only necessary details. You review the result by its impact before passing it on.

results.title: Minimise first
results.body: Remove or replace details the purpose does not need. Then carry on.
actions: Redact names, contact details and numbers

results.title: Do not enter, request approval
results.body: Without approval for exactly this combination of tool, purpose and data class you enter nothing.
actions: Ask the approval route or the responsible function
Until then work without AI or with a made-up example

results.title: Not into general assistants
results.body: Specially protected data belongs only in specialist systems approved for it; credentials go into no prompt.

results.title: Report internally at once
results.body: Report the incident through the internal channel. Secure time, tool, account, data and output; do not delete evidence on your own. The controller decides under GDPR Art. 33 whether the supervisory authority must be notified; if so, where feasible within 72 hours of becoming aware.

scenarios.text: You want to shorten an already published blog post with the approved company assistant. Tool and purpose are on the approval list.
scenarios.why: Public data, approved tool and purpose: go ahead, then proofread.

scenarios.text: You want the approved company assistant to summarise a job application including the CV. Summarising is an approved purpose.
scenarios.why: Applications are specially protected. General assistants stay blocked for them, even with an approved purpose.

scenarios.text: Yesterday a colleague copied a customer list into his private chat account.
scenarios.why: The data is already out. What counts now is the internal report, not deletion.

checks.prompt: Your office software gets a new AI writing feature through an update. May you use it with customer data straight away?

options.text: Yes, the software has already been bought.
options.feedback: Approvals cover features and configurations, not the product name.

options.text: Only once the new feature is approved for the purpose and data class.
Yes, if it is switched on by default.
options.feedback: Switched on does not mean approved. A default setting decides nothing about purpose and data class.

checks.explanation: New features in bought software are a common route into shadow AI. The combination stays blocked until it is approved.

checks.prompt: What does Article 4 of the EU AI Act require in the version in force?

options.text: A certificate for every person who uses AI.
options.feedback: Article 4 does not require a certificate.

options.text: That providers and deployers take measures that support the AI literacy of their staff, matched to context and prior knowledge.
A mandatory course with a fixed number of hours.
options.feedback: Article 4 sets neither a format nor a number of hours.

checks.explanation: Article 4 has applied since 2 February 2025 and prescribes neither a format nor a certificate. This course's record only shows that you completed this course.

lessons.title: Your team policy
lessons.subtitle: One page that helps day to day

concept.body:
An AI policy only helps if staff can apply it day to day. One page with six building blocks is enough to start, provided the approval list and procedures are maintained separately and linked:

1. **Scope:** for whom and for which tools.
2. **Approvals:** which tool for which purpose and data class.
3. **Data rules:** levels, minimisation, never credentials.
4. **Review:** review depth by impact, who signs off.
5. **Incidents:** reporting channel and what to secure.
6. **Maintenance:** who owns it and when it is reviewed.

It is finished only when every [placeholder] is replaced and the responsible functions have agreed, depending on the organization data protection, information security and the works council. It is one building block for Article 4 measures, not complete proof.
concept.takeaway: One page, six building blocks, no open placeholders: then the team can work with it.

exercise.title: Build your policy
exercise.instructions: Fill in the required fields. The preview shows the finished page; download it as Markdown or copy it.

props.template:
# AI use policy: {{org}}

Version: [date] · Owner: {{owner}}

## 1. Scope
Applies to {{scope}}, for all AI features, including in software already in use.

## 2. Approvals
{{tools}}

Any combination of tool, purpose and data class not listed here stays blocked until it is approved.

## 3. Data rules
Before every input: check data class, approval and minimisation. Enter only details the purpose needs.

Never enter:
{{never}}

## 4. Review
{{review}}. Legal statements, financial figures, decisions about people and external commitments are always signed off by the responsible person.

## 5. Incidents
Report at once via: {{incident}}. Secure time, tool, account, data and output; delete nothing on your own.

## 6. Maintenance
Review {{cycle}} and immediately after new features, contract changes, incidents or legal changes.

[Agreement: data protection, information security, works council where applicable]

fields.label: Approved tools and purposes
fields.placeholder: Company assistant: drafts of internal texts, public and internal levels

fields.label: Review rule
options: Review depth by impact: proofread, source check, specialist sign-off
Everything external under the four-eyes principle

checks.prompt: Your policy is fully drafted, but under "Incidents" it still says [reporting channel]. Is it ready for approval?

options.feedback: Without a reporting channel nobody knows where to go when it matters. This part has to be complete.

options.text: No. While a placeholder is open, nobody knows where to go when it counts.
Yes, if everyone has read it.
options.feedback: Reading it does not replace filling in the placeholders and sign-off by the responsible functions.

checks.explanation: A policy is ready for approval only when every placeholder is replaced and the responsible functions are involved.

checks.prompt: What does NOT have to be on the single page?

options.feedback: The reporting channel always belongs on the page: in an incident nobody searches attachments.

options.text: Every single tool configuration, if the approval list is maintained separately and linked.

options.feedback: Without an owner the policy goes stale. Maintenance always belongs in it.

checks.explanation: A short policy is enough if the approval list and procedures are maintained separately and clearly linked. Reporting channel and owner always belong in it.
